title: Aura Botanicals
summary: An enduring visual identity, sustainable unboxing system, and packaging suite for an organic skincare laboratory.
intro: A comprehensive brand identity and packaging project for an artisanal skincare house rooted in California flora. The goal was to express clinical efficacy while retaining an intimate, tactile connection to the earth.
overview: Aura Botanicals approached the studio to design a holistic brand architecture spanning custom logotypes, bespoke typography, glass bottle labeling, and secondary packaging crafted entirely from post-consumer recycled hemp paper.

The visual system pairs an organic emerald green palette with crisp blind-debossed white surfaces. Micro-typography was carefully calibrated across multilingual regulatory specifications without compromising visual serenity.
imageAlt: Minimalist botanical skincare packaging and visual identity in forest green and white

features.title: Modular packaging grid
features.text: A unified mathematical dieline system that accommodates twelve bottle volumes and jar dimensions effortlessly.

features.title: Blind deboss & foil stamping
features.text: Subtle tactile finishes on FSC-certified cotton paper stocks that elevate unboxing without plastic laminates.

features.title: Comprehensive brand bible
features.text: A rigorous 84-page style guide covering logotype clearances, clear zones, optical weights, and print tolerances.

approach.title: Material testing before screen design
approach.text: We sourced and tested seventeen unbleached paper stocks with master screenprinters before finalizing ink formulations.

approach.title: Typographic hierarchy under strict constraints
approach.text: FDA ingredient panels and volume disclaimers were harmonized using strict Swiss grid proportions.

approach.title: Eco-conscious production standards
approach.text: Eliminated all foil stamping foils containing petroleum plastics in favor of 100% compostable cellulose foils.

title: Kvadrat Quarterly
summary: A 180-page hardbound architectural monograph celebrating modernist spatial design and textile craft.
intro: A collector's monograph exploring the tactile intersections of brutalist architecture and woven textiles. The layout embraces deliberate asymmetry, generous margins, and exacting micro-typesetting.
overview: Kvadrat Quarterly was conceived as an object of contemplation. Printed in dual-tone deep pine and metallic silver on Fedrigoni Materica paper, the volume honors the weight of physical media.
The typographic system employs custom optical sizes, varying rhythmically between contemplative full-page imagery and dense, authoritative scholarly essays.
imageAlt: Modernist Swiss editorial publication layout and typographic grid in white and deep forest green

features.title: 12-column Swiss grid system
features.text: A mathematically proportioned grid structure that enables seamless transitions between dual-column essays and full-bleed image spreads.

features.title: Exposed Smyth-sewn binding
features.text: Lays completely flat when opened on a reading desk, preserving the visual continuity of cross-gutter architectural photographs.

features.title: Custom drop caps & glyphs
features.text: Hand-drawn architectural glyphs marking chapter transitions and bibliographic references.

approach.title: Rhythm and negative space
approach.text: Designed reader pacing with alternating moments of typographic density and calming expansive white space.

approach.title: Press-side color calibration
approach.text: Attended four-color lithographic press checks in Bologna to calibrate ink densities and black ink trap values.

approach.title: Micro-typographic rigor
approach.text: Manually kerned all headlines, adjusted tracking per font size, and refined line breaks to prevent orphans and widows.

title: Solstice Arts Festival
summary: A dynamic identity, kinetic poster series, and environmental wayfinding program for an international arts festival.
intro: Visual identity and promotional campaign for a 4-day multidisciplinary celebration of sound and light art. The visual language translates ambient waveforms into striking green geometric posters and spatial signage.
overview: Solstice needed an identity flexible enough to translate from 20-foot outdoor screenprint billboards to illuminated wayfinding totems and compact festival badges.
The solution was a generative geometric identity centered on the interaction of light waves and shadow, rendered in vibrant emerald, dark forest green, and pure white.
imageAlt: Dynamic typographic poster and geometric festival visual identity in emerald and forest green

features.title: Six-part screenprint poster series
features.text: Limited-edition silkscreen posters printed with glow-in-the-dark and metallic green inks on heavy archival paper.

features.title: Modular wayfinding language
features.text: High-contrast signage and directional iconography tested for effortless nighttime festival navigation.

features.title: Dynamic accreditation badges
features.text: Die-cut passes with security holograms and customized color coding for artists, press, and crew.

approach.title: Translating sound to geometry
approach.text: Analyzed sound frequency recordings of headlining ambient musicians to create the festival's distinctive circular wave motifs.

approach.title: Legibility at distance
approach.text: Conducted optical legibility tests at 50-meter viewing distances to ensure outdoor billboard impact.

approach.title: Sustainable exhibition materials
approach.text: Specified recyclable aluminum and unbleached cotton banners, eliminating all non-recyclable PVC vinyl.

title: Nordic Roastery
summary: Specialty coffee packaging, bespoke bespoke grotesk typeface, and retail identity for an independent roastery.
intro: A minimal, Scandinavian-inspired packaging suite and custom display font for single-origin coffees roasted in Oslo. Built around transparency, origin storytelling, and tactile unboxing.
overview: Nordic Roastery celebrates the terroir of specialty coffee. We developed a restrained visual system that allows the origin characteristics of each harvest to take center stage.
A custom geometric typeface with optical ink traps was drawn specifically for bag labels, providing distinctive presence while guaranteeing clarity at diminutive 6pt tasting note sizes.
imageAlt: Specialty coffee packaging bag and minimalist Scandinavian brand identity in deep pine and white

features.title: Custom display typeface
features.text: Nordic Grotesk: drawn with deep ink traps that maintain sharp edges even on porous kraft coffee bags.

features.title: 100% home-compostable pouch
features.text: Constructed from plant-derived PLA and barrier papers that break down naturally within 90 days.

features.title: Color-coded roast labels
features.text: A chromatic classification system using earthy tints of sage, forest, and mint to indicate processing methods.

approach.title: Type engineering in Glyphs
approach.text: Drawn from scratch to include European diacritics and specialized coffee measurement fractions.

approach.title: Moisture and aroma barrier testing
approach.text: Collaborated with barrier film engineers to protect delicate floral coffee aromas without aluminum foil.

approach.title: Streamlined packing workflow
approach.text: Designed label templates that the roastery team can overprint in-house with roast dates and batch numbers.

title: Monolith Studio
summary: Architectural brand identity, tactile stationery suite, and hardbound project portfolio monograph.
intro: Brand architecture and tactile printed stationery for a San Francisco architectural practice known for concrete residential structures and serene minimalist interior spaces.
overview: Monolith's buildings are defined by mass, honest materials, and precise geometry. We mirrored this philosophy through heavyweight 600gsm cotton letterpress stationery and a cloth-bound project folio.
The visual mark combines brutalist weight with refined proportional lines, foil stamped in deep forest green and blind-debossed into cotton stock.
imageAlt: Brutalist and minimalist architectural branding and debossed stationery in forest green and white

features.title: 600gsm duplex business cards
features.text: Ultra-thick edge-painted cards featuring a deep blind deboss that evokes the physical texture of architectural concrete.

features.title: Hardcover linen monograph
features.text: Bespoke linen-bound client presentation portfolios with foil-stamped lettering and archival photo inserts.

features.title: Architectural proposal system
features.text: A modular InDesign document template that helps partners compile technical blueprints and bids quickly.

approach.title: Material authenticity
approach.text: Selected cotton papers made from recovered textile fibers to reflect the firm's sustainable building ethos.

approach.title: Proportional harmony
approach.text: Derived all stationery dimensions and margin ratios directly from the Golden Ratio and Le Corbusier's Modulor.

approach.title: Bespoke letterpress die fabrication
approach.text: Supervised magnesium die engraving to achieve crisp 0.2mm blind debossing depth without cracking paper fibers.

title: Verve Motion Studio
summary: Kinetic visual identity, dynamic variable typography guidelines, and digital design system for a motion studio.
intro: An identity crafted for a creative studio specializing in 3D motion design and virtual spatial environments. The brand expresses continuous kinetic energy while remaining disciplined and editorial.
overview: Verve required a brand that lives naturally in motion. We designed a variable glyph system whose optical weight and curvature morph based on frame rates and user interaction.
The system bridges screen and print seamlessly, providing the motion team with guidelines for broadcast title cards, reel presentations, and printed studio promotional booklets.
imageAlt: Kinetic brand system, dynamic typography, and digital visual direction in forest green and crisp white

features.title: Dynamic variable wordmark
features.text: A brand mark that expands and contracts rhythmically in broadcast stingers and web interactions.

features.title: Motion token library
features.text: Standardized spring curves, easing timing, and spatial choreographies documented in a comprehensive design system.

features.title: Bilingual print & digital lookbook
features.text: A promotional showcase displaying the studio's cinematic reels across interactive web and tactile foil print.

approach.title: Frame-by-frame optical correction
approach.text: Refined typographic curves at each keyframe step to prevent visual weight distortion during movement.

approach.title: Design tokens in Figma
approach.text: Constructed reusable components, color styles, and type hierarchies for rapid client pitch decks.

approach.title: Cross-medium color mapping
approach.text: Mapped wide-gamut Display P3 colors to Pantone spot inks to ensure vibrant greens look identical on screen and in print.
